fields.oneLiner: BillBuddy sends a customer a WhatsApp reminder three days before an invoice is due and again on the due date, until they pay.
fields.jobStory:
BillBuddy is a smart, AI-powered invoice follow-up platform. Here is what it does:

- Create and send professional GST-compliant invoices in under 30 seconds
- Automated WhatsApp and email reminders with customisable templates
- Razorpay and UPI payment links embedded directly in every reminder
- A real-time dashboard showing paid, pending and overdue with ageing buckets
- One-click payment reconciliation so your books are always current
- Multi-user access with role-based permissions for your accountant
- Tally export so your CA does not have to re-enter anything
- Recurring invoices for retainer clients

Our target audience is small businesses across India. India has over 6.3 crore MSMEs and studies say 80% of them face delayed payments, with an average delay of 45 to 60 days. That is a huge and underserved market. Anyone who raises an invoice is a potential customer, which includes freelancers, agencies, consultants, traders, manufacturers and service businesses. We will start with small businesses and later expand to mid-market. What they do today is follow up manually, which wastes time and is unprofessional, whereas BillBuddy automates the entire receivables workflow end to end.
fields.trafficTestNotes:
Two sources, 1 to 10 September 2026.

1. Meta ads, 3,000 rupees over seven days. Audience was business page admins and people with small business interests, ages 25 to 45, all India, creative was a fifteen second screen recording of a reminder going out on WhatsApp. Ads Manager shows 34,100 impressions, 410 link clicks at 7.3 rupees a click, and 21 signups from that source.

2. A Facebook group called 'MSME Business Owners India', around 44k members. One post on 3 Sep and a comment reply thread under it. Group insights show 3,900 reach, 96 clicks to the page, 8 signups. Free.

Total spend 3,000 rupees, about 506 visits, 29 signups, 5.7% overall. That is a lot lower than I expected and I think it is because the ad audience is broad, so a lot of the clicks are curious rather than people with an actual receivables problem. Cost per signup works out to 103 rupees. The group post converted at 8.3% against the ads at 5.1%, which supports the same idea.
